description: A math-focused student who excels in theoretical logic and proofs but feels intimidated by the transition from high-level languages to C++ memory management.

nodes.personalizationRationale: This core node establishes the essential syntax foundations required for all students regardless of prior tier.
nodes.title: C++ Basics and Memory Model
nodes.description: Introduction to C++ syntax, variable scoping, and basic input/output tailored for students familiar with other high-level languages.

nodes.personalizationRationale: This student's no_prior_exposure tier necessitates specific scaffolding on pointers to transition safely from garbage-collected languages.
nodes.description: Deep dive into C++ pointers, memory addresses, and the specific syntax of references versus pointers.
nodes.title: Pointers and References Scaffolding

nodes.description: Hands-on practice with new/delete operators and the role of destructors in C++ classes.
nodes.title: Manual Memory Management Bridge
nodes.personalizationRationale: Given the student's no_prior_exposure, manual memory management is a critical friction point that requires dedicated scaffolding.
Object-oriented design is a core requirement for building complex data structures like Trees and Graphs.
nodes.title: Object-Oriented Design in C++
nodes.description: Exploration of class inheritance, access specifiers (public/private/protected), and polymorphic behavior.

nodes.personalizationRationale: As a student with no_prior_exposure, understanding template syntax early is essential for using the Goodrich/Tamassia textbook effectively.
nodes.title: Templates and Exceptions Scaffolding
nodes.description: Introduction to the syntax of function and class templates and standard C++ exception handling.

nodes.title: Linear Linked Structures
nodes.description: Implementation and comparison of Singly, Doubly, and Circularly Linked Lists.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Mastering linked structures is a fundamental requirement for the cumulative assessments in this course.

nodes.title: Recursion and Analysis (Quiz 1)
nodes.description: Evaluation of recursive algorithms and formal introduction to Big-O, Big-Omega, and Big-Theta notation.
nodes.personalizationRationale: This assessment checkpoint confirms mastery of recursion and asymptotic analysis before moving to sequence-based ADTs.
Stacks and queues are core required components of the syllabus that form the basis for tree traversals.
nodes.title: Stacks and Queues ADTs
nodes.description: Implementing Stacks and Queues using both arrays and linked lists.

nodes.title: Vectors and Iterators
nodes.description: Understanding the Vector ADT, dynamic resizing, and the abstraction of iterators.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Iterators are a core concept in C++ for traversing standard containers and custom sequences.
Sequence-based structures and initial sorting algorithms are mandatory for the cumulative midterm.
nodes.description: Sequence ADT properties and the implementation of basic sorting like Bubble Sort.
nodes.title: Sequences and Bubble Sort

nodes.description: Comprehensive review and assessment covering material from blocks 1 through 3.
nodes.title: Midterm Review & Assessment
nodes.personalizationRationale: A mandatory assessment node to ensure the student is prepared for the high-stakes midterm exam.
Tree structures represent a significant shift in data organization that is required for the final exam.
nodes.title: General Trees and Traversals
nodes.description: General tree definitions, depth, height, and standard traversal (pre-order, post-order).

nodes.personalizationRationale: Binary trees are the foundation for more advanced structures like heaps and search trees.
nodes.description: Binary tree properties, array-based and linked implementations.
nodes.title: Binary Trees Implementation

nodes.personalizationRationale: Heaps are essential for understanding efficient priority-based scheduling and sorting.
nodes.title: Priority Queues and Heaps
nodes.description: Priority Queue ADT and the implementation of Heaps using binary trees.
Hash functions, collision resolution (chaining, probing), and Map ADT interfaces.
nodes.title: Maps and Hash Tables (Quiz 3)
nodes.personalizationRationale: Maps and hash tables are mandatory topics that provide O(1) expected time for key operations.
BSTs are the prerequisite core topic for understanding balanced search trees.
nodes.description: Search properties, insertion, and deletion in Binary Search Trees.
nodes.title: Binary Search Trees
Balanced Search Trees (AVL/RB)
nodes.description: Mechanics of AVL rotations and an overview of (2,4) and Red-Black tree properties.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Balanced trees are a core, exam-tested requirement of the course syllabus.
Efficient sorting is a capstone skill that synthesizes recursion and performance analysis.
nodes.description: Divide-and-conquer sorting strategies including Merge Sort and Selection Sort analysis.
nodes.title: Sorting Algorithms (Merge/Selection)
Cumulative Final Review (Quiz 4)
nodes.description: Final synthesis of all course topics and cumulative mock exam for the final assessment.
nodes.personalizationRationale: The final review is a mandatory assessment node to prepare students for the cumulative 30% final exam.
